participants: Chris Klevan (Primal Instinct) — sales manager, ran the meeting
Andrew Jin / Andrew Musial (Primal Instinct) — closer
Kim Forbes-Sobers (Primal Instinct) — setter, code KFS
Kyla Louie (Primal Instinct) — setter, code KL
Referenced but not present: Harry Edmonds (closer, departure announced on this call), Trevor (programme owner), and prospects David, Jorge, Ricardo, Mohamed and Manny Núñez
summary: Fifty-six minute mid-week sales team meeting run by Chris Klevan. Wins round-robin, three announcements, per-person projections, then a long objection-handling training block. The announcements were a change of marketing direction to target the profile that closes best, a temporary dip in lead flow while ads are optimised, and the departure of closer Harry Edmonds by mutual agreement. A new standing policy was introduced mid-meeting: no onboarding or follow-up call goes on a calendar without a deposit first, extended to spouse objections and any money-logistics delay. The second half was a live role-play with Ben Byrne working a 'for $6,000 I could get someone in person' objection, coaching the reframe onto results, the price-as-commitment argument, and the principle that a spouse objection cannot be overcome until the prospect is certain. The setters left before the role-play. Andrew reported that Manny Núñez had no-showed the follow-up and had written to say he felt pushed and that his disclosure about his father had been used on him.
notable: NATIONALITY-BASED QUALIFICATION — the sales manager instructed the setter to apply harder financial qualification to prospects from particular countries. Chris: 'if they come from certain, like, UAE is one of those countries where I probably wouldn't hard financially qualify too much, if somebody's coming from Egypt, yeah, I probably would... if you have somebody from countries that it might be harder for them to afford things, just like, let them know, you know, just kind of give them a little bit of a harder [qualification].' Prompted by Andrew raising a UAE firefighter and 'yesterday, I had a guy from Egypt. Definitely, he didn't have the money' — that is the Ahmed Elnweshy call of 06/09.

PROSPECT-CONFIRMED PRESSURE — Manny Núñez no-showed and sent written feedback. Andrew: 'he basically said that he didn't like, at the end, that he felt pushed and used the emotions about his father and so on. Yeah, so I technically burned him.' This is direct outcome confirmation of the conduct findings on the 06/08 Manny Núñez call.

NEW DEPOSIT POLICY — Chris: 'moving forward, no onboarding calls go on the calendar unless we take a deposit', extended to 'if you get spouse objections, deposits. From now on, if you get any logistical moving money around, get a deposit... Deposits, deposits, deposits.' Amount given by example as 'a hundred bucks', described to prospects as refundable, and justified with a scarcity rationale about reserving calendar time.

CARD ON FILE — Chris: 'even if they're like, I cannot run money, be like, cool, then we'll just take down the card on file and I won't run it until this day... Because once the card's on file, we can technically just run it.'

DEPOSIT AMOUNT WITHHELD DELIBERATELY — Chris: 'I actually like to not tell them what the deposit is going to be and then see if they react terribly to it. And then I say, dude, like I could have told you it was $1. Like what's going on?... That's my favorite. They always look at me like, damn, you're right. You got me.'

PERFORMANCE GUARANTEE IS AN OFFICIAL CLOSING TOOL — Andrew: 'Would you bring up also the performance guarantee at that point?' Chris: 'Yeah, I would. I would bring it up. We're literally guaranteeing it.' Also 'when it comes to guaranteeing the results like we do'. No terms, duration, remedy or refund position was stated at any point.

PRICE AS MOTIVATION — Chris: 'the fact that it's $6,000 is actually the reason you should pay it because if you're super uncomfortable about it, you're going to [follow] through' and 'Every time you look at your bank account, use that as 6,000 reasons to actually follow through with it.' This sits directly against his own statement six minutes earlier: 'I only sell people if I know for sure they can afford it and it's not going to put them in a tight spot.'

AI CHAT BOT IN THE FUNNEL — prospects message an AI bot and reps do not always see it. Andrew on a prospect: 'I checked the sales kick, he messaged our AI bot that, I already know everything from the first call, I only need to know the price.' And on Manny: 'he actually texted also the, our AI chat bot, and I didn't see that.'

PRIMAL UNIVERSITY PAYS COMMISSION — Chris: 'you could still potentially get them in Primal University, which you will get commission for. So it's not a total, like, waste of time.' The $200/month product that sits outside the two stated tiers carries a rep incentive, which explains why it recurs as a downsell.
PROSPECT FINANCIAL DATA IS LOOKED UP BEFORE CALLS — Chris on a booked lead: 'I looked up his financial data. He's got 10K credit. He's got 106K income.' Source and basis not stated.

CASH VERSUS UNITS AGAIN — Andrew at two units for the week for $9,000 cash, an average of $4,500 per unit against the $6,000 headline. Ben declining to count a closed deal until funds land: 'I'm not going to count that Jorge guy until the money's in the account.'

HARRY EDMONDS DEPARTED — announced on this call as mutual and his own decision; he had been selling fitness a long time and wanted something more aligned. His calls appear elsewhere in the corpus, including the call the stated ICP definition is quoted from.

MARKETING RETARGETING — Chris: 'we are working on changing our marketing direction. So we can attract even more of the people that are already giving us money that we've had the highest success of closing.' Lead flow temporarily down as ads are reduced.

POSITIVE — Andrew disqualified a prospect on his own initiative and reported it as a win: 'I told him, look, this won't work for you... it would be a disservice selling you something that's already that you wouldn't use.' Kim built a free-resources template for prospects who cannot afford anything, and Chris framed it as a team value: 'Leave people better than when you found them.'

POSITIVE — Chris corrected Andrew's line 'you wouldn't be on this call if you could do it by yourself' as too aggressive: 'I think that's really strong and really direct, because you're also basically trying to push onto them that, like, dude, you can't do it on your own. But that's not true. I do believe that people can do it on their own.' He also declined to argue prospects out of cheaper alternatives: 'I'm not going to play the game of telling him, you can't find it cheap. Like, of course he can.'

The closer Andrew reported closing that day was described as roughly 60, at 9.9% body fat, a former Oracle C-level executive, using peptides, and a flat-earther. Chris: 'So you did find one of the, you sold one of these good to great guys.'
